title: The Documents letters per role are not in the P4 RBAC matrix
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.2 and T6.1; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4; Legacy RWB-E2-026 sections 10 and 16
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC1 and AC2; section 8 BR1 and BR2; section 10 Authority; section 12.8 Contract fakes
description: The TSD P4 RBAC matrix carries three columns only - Rules and parameters, Reference data and Platform administration - and no Documents column, so the letters that let a role generate a contract, credit approval or mortgage document are not stated in the technical source, although DOCUMENTS is one of the 14 LOV-CAPABILITY values. The legacy story states Documents C for the restructuring officer and the case owner, Documents R for the team manager, and generation for the SY-CASEWF identity, and those letters have to be carried as policy pack rows or the story cannot be built.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T6.1 lists 43 role rows across three capability areas and none of the columns is Documents; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 LOV-CAPABILITY carries DOCUMENTS among the 14 areas; FSD P4 v3 A2.4 gives the letter test and MSG-P4-002 but no per-role Documents row; Legacy RWB-E2-026 section 10 gives the rights and section 16 TC-E2-026-15 gives the refusal of a Documents R user.
area: Access and authority
proposed: Carry the Documents letters of the legacy authority table into the PM-2026.12 policy pack load - C for RW-RESTRUCT, RW-CASEOWN and SY-CASEWF, R for RW-TEAMMGR, no row for RW-PHONECOL - and confirm them at the policy pack review.

title: The authorise request and answer for a document generation request are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T-A.1, T-A.2 API-P4-012 and T6.2; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4 and A2.7; Legacy RWB-E2-026 sections 3, 4 and 12
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 2 to 6 and 9 to 11; section 12.1 and 12.8 Contract; section 13 Build steps 1 to 3
description: Architecture v5 names POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise as the first API path of rwb-access and says it is cached, but neither Architecture v5 nor the TSD P4 appendix T-A gives the request or the answer schema of that path. The generation request of legacy RWB-E2-026 carries the case, the treatment, one to ten template codes, the language and the Idempotency-Key, and this slice needs the case reference, the treatment reference, the template code list and the request key in the authorise request, and the letters, the roles, the scope result, the matrix version, the masking version and the field markers in the answer. None of those field names is a source value.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 14 lists REST POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA), GET /me/permissions, GET /doa-limits and /masking-policies with no schema; slide 41 gives /authorise as the first API path of rwb-access; TSD P4 T-A.1 lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and none is the authorise path, and T-A.2 API-P4-012 defines GET /me/session only; FSD P4 A2.4 gives the letter test and A2.7 gives the AC-READ and AC-DENY codes but no request shape; Legacy RWB-E2-026 section 12 defines the generation endpoint request, not the authorise request.
area: rwb-access contract
proposed: Add the authorise request and answer schema to the API specification and TSD P4 appendix T-A, publish it with RWB-P4-E1037-CON, and stub the generation facts in RWB-P5-E2026-CON so the slice can be tested before rwb-document exists.

title: The role row, class and scope of the SY-CASEWF service identity are not specified
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.2, T6.1, T6.2 and T7 NFR-051; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.30 and Requirements served REQ-ACA-010; Legacy RWB-E2-026 sections 3 and 10
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow step 4; section 7 AC4; section 10 Authority; section 13 Components
description: NFR-051 requires agents and service identities to pass the same role checks as people, and legacy RWB-E2-026 lets the case workflow identity SY-CASEWF call the generator for rule-driven generation from Epic 3, but no source gives the role row of SY-CASEWF for the DOCUMENTS capability area. TSD P4 T6.1 carries SY-CASEWF with R in Rules and parameters and R in Reference data only and has no Documents column and no scope column; LOV-ROLE-CLASS carries NON_HUMAN_ACTOR and LOV-SCOPE carries ALL, but neither is bound to this identity by any source.
evidence: TSD P4 T6.1 rows for SY-CASEWF give R, R and a dash in the three columns it carries and the second table gives R for rule packages and workflow start and signal; TSD P4 T3.2 LOV-ROLE-CLASS lists BANK_USER, PARTNER_USER and NON_HUMAN_ACTOR and LOV-SCOPE lists OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL; Legacy RWB-E2-026 section 10 says the identity calls DocumentGenerator for rule-driven generation from Epic 3 without naming a right, a class or a scope.
area: Access and authority
proposed: Add the SY-CASEWF role row to the policy pack with role_class NON_HUMAN_ACTOR, DOCUMENTS C and default_scope ALL, and record it in the reference data load with its own approver.

title: The masking version label and the DF-PTY-007 rows on the generation path are not specified
source: FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.5 and A2.7; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 masking_rule and T7 NFR-039 to NFR-042, NFR-051; Legacy RWB-E2-026 BR11
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC5; section 8 BR6 and BR7; section 11 Data; section 15 Screens and states
description: The sources fix that the national ID number DF-PTY-007 is masked on every screen and logged as masked in the access entry, and legacy RWB-E2-026 BR11 fixes that the clear value is filled at render time and exists only inside the stored PDF, but no source gives the masking version in force for SIT - MASK-SIT-01 appears once in the exception criteria of FSD P4 A2.5 with no version lifecycle - no source gives the masking_rule rows for DF-PTY-007 per role on this path, and no source fixes a mask format for a national ID number.
evidence: FSD P4 A2.5 AC-EXC-P4-004-05 names MASK-SIT-01 once and gives the date-of-birth format XXXX-XX-XX only; FSD P4 A2.7 AC-P4-007-01 lists DF-PTY-007 and DF-PTY-016 marked masked in the access entry with no rows behind them; TSD P4 T3.1 masking_rule defines role_code, field_id, unmasked, masking_version, valid_from and valid_to but carries no rows; TSD P4 T7 NFR-039 and NFR-042 state masked at rest and in use and every read logged, and no format.
area: Access and authority masking
proposed: Load the DF-PTY-007 masking rows with unmasked false for RW-RESTRUCT, RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR and SY-CASEWF under the SIT masking version, name the version in the policy pack load record, and leave the format to the one masking library every screen uses.

title: rwb-access document set: the authorise request and answer shape for the document screens, and the scope a service identity is asked for, are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 20 and 41; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 appendix T-A.1 and T6.2; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4 and A2.14; Legacy RWB-E2-017 sections 4, 10, 12 and 13
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 2 and 12; section 7 Acceptance criteria note; section 10 Authority; section 12.1, 12.2 and 12.8 Contract; section 13 Solution plan
description: (1) Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 name POST /authorise the first API path of rwb-access with GET /me/permissions, GET /doa-limits and /masking-policies, but the TSD P4 appendix T-A endpoint inventory has no authorise path and no request or answer schema, so the fields the caller sends (identity reference, roles, capability area, right, case, treatment and document references, the case owner and team for the scope test, the field ID list) and the fields the answer returns (allowed, roles, area, right, matrix version, masking version, scope result, field markers, messageId) are a read and not a source value. (2) No source states the scope a NON_HUMAN_ACTOR service identity is asked under, so the story asks it under the scope of the case it works, as NFR-051 requires of people and agents alike. (3) The per-service database login of rwb-access is named in no source; the story writes the schema and no credential.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 gives rwb-access the first API path /authorise and slide 14 lists it as an IN operation with cached; TSD P4 T-A.1 lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and none is an authorise path; TSD P4 T3.1 defines no authorise object; TSD P4 T6.2 names service identities without a scope rule; Legacy RWB-E2-017 section 12 names the document operations and no access request shape and section 13 names no login.
area: rwb-access contract and identity
proposed: Publish the authorise path with its request and answer schema in the API specification and TSD P4 appendix T-A, carry it on RWB-P4-E1037-CON and stub it in that contract fake, fix the rwb-access login in the platform DB story, and state the service identity scope rule in TSD P4 T6.2.

title: rwb-access document set: the TSD RBAC matrix has no Documents column, so the four role letters the document set needs are carried only by the legacy authority table
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.1 and T3.2; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4; Legacy RWB-E2-017 section 10
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 8 Business rules BR2 and BR3; section 10 Authority; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: The legacy story gives the four letters this slice answers: Documents CRU for RW-RESTRUCT and RW-CASEOWN, Documents R for RW-TEAMMGR and Documents CRUA for RW-LEGAL, and LOV-CAPABILITY in TSD P4 T3.2 includes DOCUMENTS as one of the 14 capability areas, so the area exists. The TSD P4 RBAC matrix tabulates only Rules and parameters, Reference data and Platform administration and gives no Documents letter for any role, so the four letters the screens ask for are taken from the legacy authority table and assumed for the policy pack, and the letter A of RW-LEGAL is recorded as the template approval of RWB-E1-034 and not as a right of this path.
evidence: TSD P4 T6.1 rows run from RW-CASEOWN Case owner to SY-AGENT Agent platform with the three column headers only; T3.2 LOV-CAPABILITY lists DOCUMENTS; Legacy RWB-E2-017 section 10 gives Documents CRU, R and CRUA per role and says no approval level applies.
area: rwb-access permission matrix
proposed: Extend the T6.1 matrix with the Documents column, confirm the four letters with the matrix owner, and publish them in the PM-2026.12 pack through RWB-P4-AD002-APP before the pack goes in force.

title: rwb-access document set: the masking version in force for SIT and the field IDs of the personal fields on the review view are not specified
source: FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.5, A2.7 and Appendix B; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 masking_rule and T7; Legacy RWB-E2-017 sections 11 and 17
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow step 5; section 7 AC2 and AC7; section 8 Business rule BR5; section 11 Data; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: No source fixes the masking version in force for SIT beyond the label MASK-SIT-01 used in the FSD P4 criteria, and no source lists the field IDs a document review view renders. The FSD P4 A2.7 access entry example names DF-PTY-007 and DF-PTY-016 as masked fields of the case record view, and the story takes those two as the party fields of the review view; any other personal field of a generated contract is unknown here, so the answer marks whatever field ID the route sends and leaves the list itself to the composite route. No mask format is fixed for either field, so the story names the field ID, the role and the version and never a rendering.
evidence: FSD P4 A2.4 AC-EXC-P4-004-05 and A2.5 use MASK-SIT-01 for a SIT example; FSD P4 A2.7 AC-P4-007-01 lists DF-PTY-007 and DF-PTY-016 as masked; TSD P4 T3.1 masking_rule gives role_code, field_id, unmasked and masking_version but no row; no source maps the merge values of a generated contract to field IDs.
area: rwb-access masking policy
proposed: Fix the mask version label per environment in the policy pack load, publish the field IDs of a generated contract and its parties with the LDM, and have the pack owner confirm the DF-PTY-007 and DF-PTY-016 rows before SIT.

title: rwb-access document set: the composite route field list of SCR-14 and SCR-30, and the decision code of an allowed screen action entry, are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 and DP-19; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.7 and A2.8; Legacy RWB-E2-017 sections 15 and 17
section: Section 5 Exception path X6; section 7 AC1, AC4 and AC8; section 8 Business rule BR9; section 12.8 Contract fakes; section 15 Screens and states
description: Architecture v5 slide 20 makes gateway-bff compose at most a few parallel calls for a screen with a 2 s timeout, but no source lists the fields the route sends to rwb-access for SCR-14 Treatment record and SCR-30 Case documents, nor how a composite screen passes a field list. The FSD P4 access log names decision codes AC-READ and AC-DENY for a case read and a refusal; no source states which code an allowed screen action such as a correction or a send carries, so the story writes AC-READ for every allowed look and action and AC-DENY for every refusal, as the FSD A2.7 and A2.8 criteria read, and records the choice here.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 20 names the composite route and its timeouts and no field list; FSD P4 A2.7 AC-P4-007-01 and A2.8 AC-P4-008-01 show AC-READ with the field IDs and masked markers, and A2.7 AC-EXC-P4-007-04 shows AC-DENY; no criterion shows a decision code for an allowed update or send; Legacy RWB-E2-017 section 17 requires personal data never in the log and names no code.
area: rwb-access access log and screen composition
proposed: Publish the composite route field list for both screens with the gateway-bff contract RWB-PLT-N001-CON and add the allowed-action decision code to the decision-code list of the ledger before the audit query is built.

title: rwb-access letter dispatch loop: the TSD RBAC matrix has no Litigation column, so the LITIGATION C and R letters the legacy authority table names are not tabulated
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.1 and T3.2; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4; Legacy RWB-E2-021 sections 10 and 12
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 Acceptance criteria AC1, AC2 and AC3; section 8 Business rules BR1 and BR2; section 10 Authority; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: The legacy authority table gives RW-LITOFF Litigation C on the request of a notice and Litigation R on its read, RW-ENFORCE Litigation CRU, and the reader roles Litigation R, and FSD A2.4 defines the matrix over the 14 capability areas of LOV-CAPABILITY, which includes LITIGATION. The TSD P4 RBAC matrix tabulates only three columns - Rules and parameters, Reference data and Platform administration - and gives no letter for any role in the Litigation area, so the letters this slice answers are carried by the PM-2026.12 policy pack rows read in this story and not by a source table.
evidence: TSD P4 T6.1 rows run 'RW-CASEOWN Case owner | R | R | -' to 'SY-AGENT Agent platform | R | R | -' under the three column headers only; LOV-CAPABILITY in T3.2 lists LITIGATION among the 14 areas; Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 10 names the letters per role and no TSD or FSD table lists a Litigation letter for any role.
area: rwb-access permission matrix
proposed: Extend the T6.1 matrix with the Litigation column for every role the legacy authority table names, publish the full 14-area matrix version as data with RWB-P4-AD002-APP, and confirm the C and R letters with the matrix owner before the pack goes in force.

title: rwb-access letter dispatch loop: the authorise request and answer shape for a notice request, a notice read and a dispatch read is not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T-A.1 and T6.2; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4 and A2.7; Legacy RWB-E2-021 sections 10 and 12
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 1, 2, 5 and 8; section 7 Acceptance criteria; section 12.1 and 12.8 Contract; section 13 Build steps 1 to 3; section 15 Screens and states
description: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 name POST /authorise as the first API path of rwb-access with GET /me/permissions, GET /doa-limits and /masking-policies, marked cached, but the TSD P4 appendix T-A endpoint inventory has no authorise path and no request or answer schema. The fields the caller sends for a notice (session identity, capability area, right C or R, the notice and case reference, the field IDs of the panel) and the fields the answer returns (allowed or denied, roles, area, right, scope applied, matrix version, masking version, field markers, message ID) are therefore a read, not a source value.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 gives rwb-access the first API path /authorise and slide 14 lists it as an IN operation 'cached'; TSD P4 T-A.1 lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and none is the authorise path; TSD P4 T3.1 defines no authorise object; Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 12 names only the P6 notice paths and the Authorization line 'Litigation, right C, scope applied'.
area: rwb-access contract
proposed: Add the authorise path with its request and answer schema to the API specification and TSD P4 appendix T-A, publish it with RWB-P4-E1037-CON and stub it in that contract fake, and add the access entry decision codes to the ledger code list.

title: rwb-access letter dispatch loop: the masking version in force in SIT, the field IDs of the addressee postal address and party field on the notice panel, and the composite route field list are not specified
source: FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.5, A2.7 and Appendix B; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 masking_rule and T7; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20; Legacy RWB-E2-021 sections 11, 15 and 17
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 Acceptance criteria AC3 and AC6; section 11 Data; section 15 Screens and states; section 17 Guardrails
description: Three values are absent. (1) The masking_rule rows name a masking_version, but no source fixes which version is in force in SIT; this story assumes MASK-SIT-01, the label FSD P4 v3 uses in its own examples. (2) FSD P4 v3 A2.7 AC-P4-007-01 marks DF-PTY-007 and DF-PTY-016 masked on the case record view and no source states which field ID is the addressee postal address on the notice panel or which second party field the panel carries, nor any mask format for a postal address. (3) The gateway-bff composite route behind SCR-18 and SCR-04 has no published field list, so the field list the panel sends in the authorise request is a read.
evidence: FSD P4 A2.7 AC-P4-007-01 lists DF-PTY-007 and DF-PTY-016 as 'masked' and A2.5 AC-EXC-P4-004-05 shows a date of birth as 'XXXX-XX-XX' with no postal address example; TSD P4 T3.1 masking_rule has field_id varchar(16) and masking_version varchar(20) with no value list; Appendix B refers to the Design System and Component Library and fixes no rendering; Arch v5 slide 20 describes the composite route without a field list.
area: rwb-access masking policy and screen composition
proposed: Fix the masking version in force per environment in the policy pack load, publish the field ID of the addressee postal address and of the party field with the mask format in the data dictionary, and publish the composite route field list for SCR-18 and SCR-04 with gateway-bff (DP-19).

title: rwb-access letter dispatch loop: the role code and scope of the service identity that runs JOB-10 are not specified
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.1, T6.2 and T7 NFR-051; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 41 and 44; Legacy RWB-E2-021 sections 10 and 12
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 Acceptance criteria AC5; section 8 Business rules BR6; section 10 Authority; section 11 Data; section 13 Components
description: NFR-051 requires that agents run under service identities subject to the same role checks as people, and the legacy authority table names 'the recovery service identity' as the actor that runs JOB-10 and reads the proof rows from v_ace_pod, with no role code and no scope. TSD P4 T6.1 lists the service identities SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-DATALOAD, SY-OCR and SY-AGENT and none of them is the runner of JOB-10, so the role code of that identity and the scope it holds for the Litigation read of a notice are a read, not a source value.
evidence: TSD P4 T7 NFR-051 states the principle only; TSD P4 T6.1 tabulates SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-DATALOAD, SY-OCR and SY-AGENT with R letters in three areas and no Litigation column; Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 10 names 'The recovery service identity' without a code, and Arch v5 slide 44 gives JOB-10 to rwb-comms with rwb-integration without naming an identity.
area: rwb-access role model and service identity
proposed: Name the service identity of the JOB-10 runner in the role table with role class NON_HUMAN_ACTOR, scope ALL and its Litigation R row, and record it in the policy pack load of RWB-P4-AD002-APP.

title: The Documents letters per role are not carried by the P4 access documents
source: Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; legacy RWB-E2-024

description: TSD P4 v3 T6.1 carries three columns only - Rules and parameters, Reference data and Platform administration - and FSD P4 v3 A2.4 gives the permission table's fields with no row per role. The legacy authority table is therefore the only source of the Documents letters: RW-FIELDCOL CR, RW-CASEOWN CRU, RW-RESTRUCT CRU, SY-OCR CRU and RW-PHONECOL R. evidence: TSD P4 v3 T6.1 column header 'Role | Rules and parameters | Reference data | Platform administration'; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 LOV-CAPABILITY lists DOCUMENTS among the 14 areas; legacy RWB-E2-024 section 10 'RW-FIELDCOL ... Documents CR' and 'RW-PHONECOL ... Documents R'; no Documents column in either P4 document
area: Access and authority (P4 rwb-access); permission matrix
owner_role: Security administrator with the P4 business analyst
proposed: Add the five DOCUMENTS rows to the permission file of the PM-2026.12 load under the policy pack path (RWB-P4-AD002-APP), and carry a Documents column in the TSD P4 RBAC matrix so the letters have a written home beside the three columns it has today

title: The masking rows and the mask version for the capture position are not specified
source: Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; legacy RWB-E2-024; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary
section: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 masking_rule (DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204); FSD P4 v3 A2.5 and AC-EXC-P4-004-05; legacy RWB-E2-024 BR9; DF-DOC-028 and DF-DOC-029

FSD P4 v3 names MASK-SIT-01 only inside examples for v_ace_customer.date_of_birth, an identity number and a phone number, and gives no rendering for a coordinate. The story therefore answers the two position fields from assumed rows for RW-CASEOWN and RW-RESTRUCT, names the version, and asserts only that a field is masked or unmasked and that no value is present.

area: Access and authority (P4 rwb-access); masking
owner_role: Compliance and PDPA officer with the P4 solution architect
proposed: Record the DF-DOC-028 and DF-DOC-029 rows per role in the MASK-SIT-01 pack, with unmasked true for RW-CASEOWN and RW-RESTRUCT, false for RW-FIELDCOL and RW-PHONECOL and no row for SY-OCR, and let the platform masking library own one rendering per field type

title: The Case record letters per role are not in the TSD P4 role-to-permission matrix
source: Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 022 SMS and LINE dispatch through NSS and LINE OA v1.md
section: TSD P4 v3 T6.1 RBAC matrix (three columns: Rules and parameters, Reference data, Platform administration); FSD P4 v3 A2.4; legacy RWB-E2-022 section 10 (Authority)
description: The TSD P4 role to permission matrix carries three capability areas only, and Case record is not one of them. The letters this slice decides on - Case record C for RW-CASEOWN and R for RW-TEAMMGR, RW-CONDUCT and RW-COMPLAIN - come from the legacy story's authority table and from the FSD P4 examples, which name the area CASE_RECORD for a break-glass grant and a refusal but publish no matrix row. No source states whether any other role holds a Case record letter, so a new role cannot be placed without a row.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T6.1 columns 'Rules and parameters | Reference data | Platform administration' with 40 role rows under them; FSD P4 v3 AC-ALT-P4-007-01 area 'CASE_RECORD' and AC-EXC-P4-007-04 area 'PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION'; legacy RWB-E2-022 section 10 rows 'RW-CASEOWN ... (Case record C)' and 'RW-TEAMMGR ... (Case record R)'
area: Access and authority (P4 rwb-access); permission matrix
owner_role: Security administrator with the P4 solution architect
proposed: Add the Case record column, and the other capability areas the stories decide on, to the role to permission matrix of TSD P4 before the first SIT entry, and load the letters as PM-2026.12 rows so that no story holds a letter of its own

title: The masking version in force and the unmask rows for DF-ACE-078 and DF-ACE-077 are not recorded
source: Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8
section: FSD P4 v3 A2.5 AC-ALT-P4-005-01 and AC-EXC-P4-005-05; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 masking_rule DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204; LDM v8 DF-ACE-077 and DF-ACE-078
description: The masking version appears only inside two FSD criteria that name MASK-SIT-01 for a SIT example, and no load record, environment table or pack manifest states which version is in force, who approved it or its valid-from date. title: The rights of the JOB-11 service identity and the decision code of a send are not recorded
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md; Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md
section: Arch v5 slide 44 (JOB-11 Outbox sender, every minute, every service) and slide 41 (rwb-access owns the access log); Temporal and Drools design slide 12 and slide 32 note 6 (jobs as Schedules, no Quartz); FSD P4 v3 A2.7 and A2.8 decision codes AC-READ, AC-DENY and AC-EXPT
